I created `src/exports/jsonlExport.ts`. It exports `exportJsonl(jobId, batchId)`, which loads the batch with `loadBatch`, writes one JSON object per line, and uploads to the sink under `${jobId}.jsonl`. It also exports a `toJsonl(rows)` helper, like `toCsv` in the CSV export. I haven't run it or type-checked it.

It uses the same fields and snake_case names as the CSV export: `id`, `batch_id`, `prompt`, `response` and `rating`. It leaves out `labCustomerId` and `createdAt`, as the CSV does. If you want them in the JSONL output, say so and I'll add them.

I didn't touch `scheduler.ts`. `ExportJob.format` already allows `"jsonl"`, but I didn't check whether the scheduler dispatches to `exportJsonl`.
